name: The Estuary Day
location: Thames estuary, Kent and Essex shores
summary: One long day: twenty-two miles along the estuary with eighty others, walking in changing pairs and talking the whole way. Facilitators at each stage. First-timers make up most of the day. £240.
description:
Once a month from March to October, eighty people walk twenty-two miles along the estuary from the marshes to the sea, in pairs, talking.

The form is simple. You are given a partner at the start and a question. You walk and talk for an hour. At the first stage, a hut or a sea wall or a pub garden, you swap partners and get a new question. Eight stages, eight partners, eight questions, and the sea at the end. What you talk about is not prescribed beyond the question and people go where they go.

There is no leader. At each stage two facilitators hand out the next question, keep the clock, and are there if a conversation has gone somewhere difficult and someone wants a third person for ten minutes. Otherwise the day is yours and your partners'. Which path you take between stages, how fast, whether you stop, is up to the pair.

It is a hard day. Twenty-two miles is a long way on legs that do not usually do it, the estuary wind is relentless, and eight hours of honest conversation is tiring in a way people do not anticipate. Bring the right boots.

Most people who come have never done anything like it, and the day is built for that. The first stage is a short one and the facilitators there explain how it works and what to do if you do not know what to say. Nobody is expected to arrive knowing anything.
practical: One Saturday a month, March to October, 7am start, finish around 5pm. £240 including transport back from the sea, a packed lunch, and the facilitation. Eighty places. Bring walking boots you have worn in, waterproofs, water, and a change of socks. Start point is a ten-minute walk from Gravesend station. Mobile signal throughout.
